problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-5\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6y=6{e}^{3x}.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Inhomogeneous ODEs With Exponential Forcing

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+6\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+8y=2{e}^{-4x}
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-2x}+B{e}^{-4x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the complementary function is ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-2x}+B{e}^{-4x},$ the roots of the auxiliary equation are $\lambda =-2$ and $\lambda =-4.$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $2{e}^{-4x}.$ In this case, the constant factor in the exponent is $-4$, which coincides with one of the roots of the auxiliary equation. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha x{e}^{-4x}.
$$

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=\alpha (1-4x){e}^{-4x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=\alpha (16x-8){e}^{-4x}.
$$

We substitute ${y}_{p},$ ${y}_{p}^{′},$ and ${y}_{p}^{″}$ into the ODE and solve for $\alpha :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha (16x-8){e}^{-4x}+6(\alpha (1-4x){e}^{-4x})+8(\alpha x{e}^{-4x}) & =2{e}^{-4x} \\ (16x-8+6-24x+8x)\alpha {e}^{-4x} & =2{e}^{-4x} \\ -2\alpha {e}^{-4x} & =2{e}^{-4x} \\ -2\alpha  & =2 \\ \alpha  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-x{e}^{-4x}.
$$
